transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2027-07-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood CS), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (CTO, Rivermist Health), Mark Reynolds (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Security Lead)

Summary: 
Quick kickoff for onboarding Rivermist to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with focus areas: VPC/private deployment, SSO/KMS, pilot timeline, and success metrics. Agreed next steps around workshop and checklist.

Topics: 
- Goals and success criteria
- Security/compliance requirements (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
- Network and VPC considerations
- Pilot scope and timeline
- Roles and communication channels

Action items (captured verbally in call) - see metadata field for owners/dates.

Transcript body: 
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Uh, we're really excited to get Rivermist onboarded. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here. CTO. Thanks Jordan.
[00:09] Mark: Mark, platform. Hey.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:13] Samir: Samir from Redwood, SE, hi all.
[00:15] Jordan: Perfect. So objective is to get you to a staged pilot in production-like conditions within four weeks, um -- is that still the target?
[00:25] Aisha: Yeah that's what execs want, four to six weeks is ideal, sooner if possible. Cost is a thing but timeline is priority.
[00:33] Mark: We'll need dedicated capacity because of peak inference loads, and also the egress constraints from our VPC are strict.
[00:40] Samir: Cool, we can do Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment. We typically recommend Dedicated reserved pool for initial pilots for predictability.
[00:48] Priya: On security, we need SOC 2, SAML SSO, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[00:57] Jordan: Yep those are standard ask. We'll share SSO docs and our KMS integration playbook. Samir, do you want to run through the typical onboarding steps?
[01:05] Samir: Sure. Step one is account setup and RBAC -- you'll get an org owner and team roles. Then network setup -- VPC peering, setup egress rules and firewall ports, and we'll provision a staging dedicated pool. We'll also need sample traffic and prompts for performance tuning.
[01:23] Mark: Sample traffic, yeah we can synthesize load and also provide representative prompt sets. We use a lot of short chats and some long-form summarization so sequence length varies.
[01:32] Samir: Good to know. That affects batching and kernel selection. Also, on KV cache, sorry KV cache, um sometimes our transcripts show K V cash, but it's KV cache, that matters for latency.
[01:45] Priya: For encryption, do you support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM?
[01:50] Samir: Yes, we support KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated via CMKs; for on-prem HSM we have an adapter. We'll share docs. Note: if you require FIPS mode we need to check the specific kernel builds.
[02:03] Aisha: Can you give a rough latency/cost profile for our expected loads? We want p99 under 400ms for short queries.
[02:10] Jordan: We'll run initial benchmarks; typical short-chat p99 on Dedicated is around 200-350ms depending on model and quantization. We'll propose a model/quantization config and a cost estimate.
[02:21] Mark: Model selection - are you recommending an open model? Some of our compliance folks prefer no external closed models.
[02:27] Samir: We have a catalog. For latency-first, a quantized 7B variant often hits price/latency targets. If you need higher quality, we can pick a larger model, but cost goes up.
[02:37] Priya: About data residency - our PHI data must stay in region. Can Dedicated be pinned to a region?
[02:43] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated can be region pinned and Private is fully in-customer network. We'll note this in the checklist.
[02:50] Aisha: Great. On timelines, what's the critical path?
[02:54] Samir: Network and security approvals typically take the longest. If you can get us network diagrams and the list of firewall rules, Samir: we'll provision staging in parallel.
[03:05] Mark: I'll share the network diagram by early next week.
[03:08] Jordan: Awesome. Also we'll provide an onboarding playbook link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/rivermist (note: placeholder).
[03:18] Aisha: Sounds good. One of the things we want is canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes.
[03:25] Samir: Yep, our rollout policies support canary and auto-fallback to compatible model variants. We'll demo that in the deep-dive.
[03:33] Priya: For audit logs, can we stream them to Splunk?
[03:36] Jordan: Yes, we can forward audit logs; we'll share the schema and sample events.
[03:41] Mark: Any blocker on SAML? We use Okta.
[03:44] Samir: Okta is supported; we need IdP metadata and attributes. We'll add that to the checklist.
[03:51] Aisha: Good. Ok next, who owns which deliverables?
[03:55] Jordan: I'll own the onboarding checklist and project coordination. Samir will own the technical setup. Mark and Priya you'll be the customer leads for network and security.
[04:06] Priya: Yep.
[04:07] Mark: Yep.
[04:08] Jordan: Any questions from the team?
[04:10] Aisha: Do you have references for other health customers?
[04:13] Jordan: We can share anonymized case studies and references; also a contact for another health customer who did a private deployment.
[04:20] Aisha: Great.
[04:22] Samir: Ok, let's sketch timeline: this week - checklist and docs, next week - network peering and staging provision, week after - pilot run and latency tuning, week 4 - go/no-go for production rollout.
[04:35] Mark: That works. What's the expected time for provisioning the dedicated pool?
[04:38] Samir: Typically 48-72 hours after network access is confirmed.
[04:41] Mark: Good.
[04:43] Jordan: We'll send pricing estimates too; note that reserved commits reduce unit cost and we can show Dedicated price windows.
[04:50] Aisha: Ok we'll review budget.
[04:53] Priya: One last security note: need the list of sub-processors and data flow doc for legal.
[04:58] Jordan: We'll attach sub-processor list and DPA template.
[05:02] Aisha: Perfect.
[05:03] Jordan: Wrapping up, can we confirm the next meeting? Deep-dive workshop - propose 2027-08-03 at 15:00 UTC.
[05:12] Mark: Works for me.
[05:14] Priya: Works.
[05:16] Samir: I'll send the invite.
[05:17] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone.
[05:20] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hears, e.g., "K V cash" instead of "KV cache". Links shared: onboarding playbook (placeholder), SSO guide (to be sent), security docs (DPA and subprocessor list).

End of transcript.
